questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to stay safe at big football matches
Why crowds affect us and how we behave in them
The biggest religious festivals in India
How trains can carry more passengers safely
questions.why: Sam says they'll discuss the role of crowds and why they evoke different reactions in people.

questions.q: Why does Sam feel differently about the football crowd?
options: It is smaller than the station crowd
She always has a seat there
It is quieter
It feels more like a big group of friends
questions.why: She says that's different – 'more like a big group of friends'.

questions.q: Which older idea about crowds does Professor John Drury describe?
options: People in crowds become calmer and wiser
Crowds always make people feel happy and safe
Crowds make people gullible and violent
Crowds help people make better decisions
questions.why: He says in crowds people supposedly regress, become more gullible and tend towards violence.

questions.q: What does research say about the idea of 'mob mentality', according to Anand Jagatia?
options: It is not supported by research
It explains most crowd behaviour
It is true only at football matches
It has never been studied
questions.why: He says the idea of mob mentality 'just isn't backed up by research'.

questions.q: According to Dr Anne Templeton, what makes a crowd more enjoyable?
options: Being with very few people around you
Having a lot of police officers around
Standing near the exit so you can leave
Feeling part of a group with the others
questions.why: She says the more people feel part of a group with others in the crowd, the more they enjoy it.

questions.q: What do people expect when they feel part of a group, according to Dr Templeton?
options: That others will look after them
That others will push them
That they must lead the group
That the event will end early
questions.why: She says if we feel in a group with others, we expect them to look after us.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention football fans wearing the same colours and singing?
options: To show how noisy big football matches can be
To explain why rival fans often start fights
To show how shared identity bonds a crowd
To say that fans spend too much money on shirts
questions.why: He says it works as a kind of glue, bonding the crowd and making them feel safe.

questions.q: According to Neil, why are crowds important today?
options: They help people find jobs and new friends
Together, people feel they have power
They are always safer than being alone
They are good places to watch sport on TV
questions.why: He says crowds give us power, like marching together feeling you could change the world.
